mainTopic: The measuring vessels of the מקדש: the dry עשרון measures and the dispute of רבי מאיר and חכמים, רמי בר חמא's three questions, and the seven liquid measures.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about the dry measures in the מקדש. רבי מאיר holds there were two עשרון vessels. חכמים say there was only one עשרון, and they read the doubled 'עשרון עשרון' as adding a half-עשרון vessel. The גמרא shows that each side uses every part of the פסוקים, with differences over whether to learn from an extra ו or from the dots in the Torah. Next, רב ששת explains that the half-עשרון vessel did not measure each half from scratch. It only divided the כהן גדול's full tenth into two halves. רמי בר חמא then asks רב חסדא three questions. Was the half-עשרון heaped or leveled? Leveled. Were the חביתין divided by hand or with a vessel? By hand, since weighing bread recalls a curse. Does the שלחן make holy קמצים placed on it? Only enough for them to become פסול, not enough to be offered. Finally, a new משנה lists seven liquid measures in the מקדש, with different views from רבי אליעזר בר רבי צדוק and רבי שמעון. The גמרא begins with a ברייתא giving the lists of רבי יהודה, רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון, and רבי שמעון's words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The leveled measure was used for the High Priest's daily offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר finishes his statement: the leveled עשרון vessel was the one used to measure flour for the חביתי כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leveled one was the vessel used to measure the flour for the High Priest's griddle-cake offering.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא in the middle of רבי מאיר's words. He has described two עשרון vessels, and now he says the leveled one was used for the כהן גדול's daily offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר there were two separate vessels that each held a tenth of an איפה. One of them, the leveled (מחוק) one, had a special job: measuring flour for the חביתין of the כהן גדול. This sets up the disagreement of חכמים in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Leveled: filled only to the rim, with the top wiped flat.
The griddle-cake מנחה the כהן גדול brought every day.
A tenth of an איפה, a standard measure of flour.

phrases.english: The leveled one was the vessel with which he would measure
for the High Priest's griddle-cake offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי מאיר's statement in the ברייתא from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי מאיר's view, the leveled עשרון vessel was used for the חביתי כהן גדול.

steps.title: חכמים say there was only one tenth-measure
steps.stepSummary: חכמים argue that the מקדש had only one עשרון vessel, and they bring the פסוק 'ועשרון אחד לכבש האחד' as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים say: there was only one tenth-measure there, as it says: 'And one tenth-part for every lamb.'
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. They say there was just one עשרון vessel, and they bring a פסוק that says 'one'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים read the word 'אחד' (one) in the פסוק as telling us how many עשרון vessels there were: one. That goes directly against רבי מאיר's two vessels. The next step will press on how חכמים explain the doubled 'עשרון עשרון'.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that disagrees with רבי מאיר here.
As it is said: introduces a פסוק used as proof.
A lamb, here one of the קרבנות brought with a מנחה.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה שָׁם אֶלָּא עִשָּׂרוֹן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: There was only one tenth-measure there,
as it is said: "And one tenth-part
for every lamb."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר's two vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one עשרון measuring vessel was in the מקדש, learned from 'עשרון אחד'.

steps.title: Then what does the doubled 'tenth, tenth' teach?
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, the question is raised: if there was only one עשרון, why does the פסוק say 'עשרון עשרון' twice?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the verse mean by saying 'a tenth, a tenth'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks חכמים a question. If there was only one עשרון, why does the תורה repeat the word? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר learned two vessels from this doubled word. Now that חכמים say there was only one, the repetition needs a new explanation, or it looks like it has no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your view is correct, then...
What does the verse come to teach? Asked when a word looks extra.

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying
"A tenth, a tenth"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how חכמים explain the doubled word that רבי מאיר used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What חכמים learn from the repeated 'עשרון עשרון'.

steps.title: The doubled word adds a half-tenth vessel
steps.stepSummary: חכמים answer that the repeated 'עשרון' comes to include another vessel, a חצי עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a half-tenth measure.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים answer the question: the extra 'עשרון' teaches that there was also a vessel holding half a tenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So חכמים don't ignore the repetition. They use it for something else: not a second full עשרון, but a smaller half-עשרון vessel. Both sides now agree there was a half-עשרון vessel; they only argue about where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: To include: the verse adds something extra.
Half a tenth of an איפה, a smaller measuring vessel.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: two עשרון vessels (from 'עשרון עשרון'). חכמים: one עשרון (from 'עשרון אחד'), and 'עשרון עשרון' adds a half-עשרון vessel.

phrases.english: To include a half-tenth measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'עשרון עשרון'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repetition includes a חצי עשרון measuring vessel.

steps.title: Where does רבי מאיר get the half-tenth from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since רבי מאיר uses 'עשרון עשרון' for two full vessels, how does he know about a half-עשרון vessel?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר: from where does he get the half-tenth?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is over, and now the גמרא discusses it. It asks רבי מאיר's source for the half-עשרון vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים got the half-עשרון from the doubled word. רבי מאיר already used that doubled word for his second full vessel, so he needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it? Asks for a source.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir,
from where does he derive the half-tenth?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, חֲצִי עִשָּׂרוֹן מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא, the גמרא begins examining each opinion, starting with רבי מאיר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי מאיר's source for a חצי עשרון vessel.

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns it from the extra 'and'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns the half-עשרון from the letter ו in 'וְעשרון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He derives it from 'And a tenth'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר learns the half-עשרון from the small word 'and' (the letter ו) at the start of 'ועשרון'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats the extra letter ו as adding something, and here it adds the half-עשרון vessel. So he has a source for the half vessel without using the doubled word.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it: he learns it from this source.
The letter ו, meaning 'and', sometimes used to add a teaching.

phrases.english: He derives it from "And a tenth."
phrases.notes: He means the ו at the start of 'ועשרון אחד' in the פסוק the חכמים quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי מאיר's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ו in 'ועשרון' includes the חצי עשרון.

steps.title: חכמים do not expound the letter 'and'
steps.stepSummary: חכמים don't learn the half-עשרון from the ו, because they don't learn anything from an extra ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים do not expound a ו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why חכמים don't use the ו like רבי מאיר does: in their view a single extra ו is not enough to learn from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a difference in how to read פסוקים. רבי מאיר learns from an extra ו and חכמים do not. That is why חכמים needed the doubled 'עשרון עשרון' to get the half-עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: They don't expound: they don't learn a law from it.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis do not expound a "vav."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why חכמים don't use the ו too.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חכמים do not learn anything from an extra ו.

steps.title: What does רבי מאיר do with 'one tenth for each lamb'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר learns from 'ועשרון אחד לכבש האחד', the פסוק חכמים used to prove there was only one vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר: what does he do with this verse, 'And one tenth-part for every lamb'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: since רבי מאיר holds there were two vessels, what does he learn from the פסוק that says 'one tenth'? The answer is in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר used only the ו of this פסוק. The rest of it, which חכמים read as 'only one vessel', still needs a purpose in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? What does he learn from this verse?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir, this verse:
"And one tenth-part for every lamb"
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַאי ״וְעִשָּׂרוֹן אֶחָד לַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to רבי מאיר and asks about the פסוק חכמים used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי מאיר learns from 'עשרון אחד לכבש האחד'.

steps.title: Measure one tenth at a time, not with a bigger vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns from the פסוק that you may not measure the flour for a bull or a ram with one large vessel of three or two tenths.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse teaches that one should not measure with a three-tenths vessel for a bull, nor with a two-tenths vessel for a ram.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: for רבי מאיר, the פסוק teaches how to measure. You use the one-עשרון vessel again and again, never one big vessel holding the whole amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bull's מנחה needs three tenths and a ram's needs two tenths. The פסוק stresses 'one tenth', which teaches that each tenth is measured on its own with the עשרון. So רבי מאיר still uses the word 'אחד', just for a different law than חכמים do.

keyTerms.meaning: That one should not measure.
A bull, whose מנחה is three tenths.
A ram, whose מנחה is two tenths.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use every part of the פסוקים. רבי מאיר: 'עשרון עשרון' means two vessels, the ו adds a half-עשרון, and 'עשרון אחד' means measure one tenth at a time. חכמים: 'עשרון אחד' means one vessel, 'עשרון עשרון' adds a half-עשרון, and they don't learn from a ו.

phrases.english: That verse teaches that one should not measure
neither with a three-tenths vessel for a bull,
nor with a two-tenths vessel for a ram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what רבי מאיר learns from 'עשרון אחד'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that each tenth is measured separately, never with a three-tenths or two-tenths vessel.

steps.title: חכמים learn the rule from the dotted ו
steps.stepSummary: חכמים learn that one may not measure with a three-tenths or two-tenths vessel from the dot over the ו in 'עשרון', as רבי יוסי teaches in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים? They learn this rule from the dots. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said: Why is the ו in the middle of the first 'עשרון' in the פסוק of the first day of סוכות dotted? To teach that one should not measure flour with a three-tenths vessel for a bull or with a two-tenths vessel for a ram.
steps.whatsHappening: In step 9, רבי מאיר learned the 'no big vessel' rule from a פסוק that חכמים use for something else. The גמרא now shows where חכמים get that same rule: from the dots over the word עשרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on the rule itself. They only disagree on its source. For חכמים, the dot over the ו in the סוכות פסוק teaches that each tenth must be measured separately, so you cannot use one big vessel for the bull's three tenths or the ram's two tenths.

keyTerms.meaning: Dots written above letters in the Torah scroll, which can be used to teach a law
They learn it from (literally, 'it comes out for them')
A tenth of an איפה, the basic flour measure for a מנחה
A bull, whose מנחה needs three tenths of flour
A ram, whose מנחה needs two tenths of flour

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, they derive it from the dots,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule from step 9: no measuring with a big three-tenths or two-tenths vessel.

phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
Why is the vav in the middle of "issaron" dotted
in the first "issaron"

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג?
phrases.english: of the first festival day of the Festival?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יִמְדּוֹד לֹא בְּשֶׁל שְׁלֹשָׁה לְפַר
phrases.english: So that one should not measure, neither with a three-tenths vessel for a bull,
nor with a two-tenths vessel for a ram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים' source for the same rule רבי מאיר learned in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do חכמים learn the 'no big vessel' rule?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the dot over the ו in 'עשרון', as רבי יוסי teaches.

steps.title: רבי מאיר does not learn from dots
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר does not learn anything from the dots, so he needs the פסוק from step 9 for this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר does not learn anything from dots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי מאיר does not use the dotted ו: he does not learn laws from dots at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the loop. רבי מאיר needs 'ועשרון אחד לכבש האחד' for the 'no big vessel' rule because he does not treat dots as a source. חכמים do learn from dots, which leaves that פסוק free to teach that there was only one vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Learns a law from (a word, letter or mark in the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on the rule against measuring with one big vessel. רבי מאיר learns it from 'ועשרון אחד לכבש האחד', while חכמים learn it from the dotted ו.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir does not derive anything from dots.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי מאיר does not use the חכמים' source from step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי מאיר do with the dot?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Nothing. He does not learn from dots.

steps.title: The משנה: the half-tenth measured the High Priest's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the half-עשרון vessel was used to measure flour for the כהן גדול's חביתין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the half-tenth vessel used for? It was used to measure the flour for the כהן גדול's griddle-cake offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה about what the half-עשרון vessel was for. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול brought a tenth of flour every day, half in the morning and half in the afternoon. The משנה's word 'measure' sounds like each half was measured on its own with the half-tenth vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel that holds half a tenth
The daily griddle-cake מנחה of the כהן גדול, offered half in the morning and half in the afternoon
Measures

phrases.english: The half-tenth: what was it used for?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבּוֹ הָיָה מוֹדֵד לַחֲבִיתֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל.
phrases.english: With it one would measure for the High Priest's griddle-cake offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The half-עשרון vessel was used to measure the כהן גדול's חביתין.

steps.title: Contradiction: the High Priest brought a whole tenth and split it
steps.stepSummary: Another משנה says the חביתין were not brought as halves. A whole tenth was brought and then divided, so why would the half-tenth vessel be needed for measuring?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really 'measure' with it? There is a contradiction: The כהן גדול's griddle-cake offering was not brought in halves. Instead, he brings a complete tenth and divides it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה with another משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a full tenth is measured first and then split, the half-tenth vessel is never used to measure the amount. That seems to clash with our משנה's word 'measure'.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction to it (one source set against another)
Halves
He divides it in half

phrases.english: Measure? And contrast this with the following:

phrases.aramaic: חֲבִיתֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל לֹא הָיוּ בָּאִין חֲצָאִין,
phrases.english: The High Priest's griddle-cake offering did not come in halves,
rather, he brings a complete tenth and divides it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the half-עשרון was used to measure the חביתין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה says a whole tenth is brought and then divided, so the half vessel is not used to measure.

steps.title: רב ששת: 'Measure' means 'divide'
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that 'measure' in our משנה means dividing the full tenth into two equal halves using the half-tenth vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: What does 'measure', which the משנה teaches, mean? It means 'divide'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת resolves the contradiction by reading the word 'measure' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full tenth is measured first, as the other משנה says. Then the half-tenth vessel is used to split it into two equal portions. So both משניות agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Divides

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול's tenth is measured whole, and the half-tenth vessel is used only to divide it into morning and afternoon halves.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the half-tenth vessel measured each half from scratch. The full tenth comes first, and the half vessel only splits it.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
What is the meaning of "measure" that it teaches?
Divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מַאי ״מוֹדֵד״ נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Measure' meant each half was measured separately with the half vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Measure' means dividing a whole tenth into halves, which fits the other משנה.

steps.title: Was the half-tenth vessel heaped or leveled?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא whether, according to רבי מאיר, the חצי עשרון vessel measured heaped or leveled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: According to רבי מאיר, was the half-tenth vessel a heaped measure or a leveled measure?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רמי בר חמא wants to know whether the half-tenth vessel was meant to be filled heaped over the top or leveled off flat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds there were two עשרון vessels, one גדוש and one מחוק. Since the עשרון came in both kinds, it is natural to ask which kind the חצי עשרון was.

keyTerms.meaning: The vessel holding half of a tenth of an איפה
Heaped: filled until the flour piles above the rim
Leveled: filled and then wiped flat with the rim

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked Rav Ḥisda:
The half-tenth vessel, according to Rabbi Meir,
was it heaped, or was it leveled?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the half-tenth vessel was used (step 14) to what kind of measure it was.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר's half-tenth vessel was a heaped or leveled measure.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming questions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן: half, griddle-cakes, table, to help remember the order of the questions in this series.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: Half, griddle-cakes, Table.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to give a memory aid for the series of questions it is about to present. This is setup, not an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one question: the half-tenth vessel, the כהן גדול's חביתין, and the שלחן. It keeps the order of the questions straight.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid that lists the topics coming up
The כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering (חביתין)
The Table in the מקדש that held the לחם הפנים

phrases.english: (A memory aid:
Half, griddle-cakes, Table.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interrupts the question to give a memory aid for the whole series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three questions follow: half-tenth, חביתין, שלחן.

steps.title: Why ask only according to רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the question is limited to רבי מאיר. Couldn't it also be asked according to חכמים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But ask the question according to חכמים too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes back on how רמי בר חמא framed his question. Why mention only רבי מאיר, when חכמים also have a half-tenth vessel?
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים agree there was a half-tenth vessel in the מקדש. So the same heaped-or-leveled question seems to apply to them, and naming רבי מאיר alone looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'and let it be asked by you': why not ask it this way too?
The Sages, who disagree with רבי מאיר here

phrases.english: But let the question be asked according to the Rabbis too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the way step 15's question was framed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the question is limited to רבי מאיר's view.

steps.title: For חכמים, the question starts with the tenth itself
steps.stepSummary: According to חכמים, the open question would be about the עשרון vessel itself, so the half-tenth question belongs specifically to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to חכמים, they would first be asking about the tenth vessel itself: was it heaped or leveled?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא explains why his question named רבי מאיר. For חכמים, even the main tenth vessel is unclear, so the half-tenth question would come later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר clearly had one heaped עשרון and one leveled עשרון, so for him only the half-tenth is unclear. חכמים had just one עשרון, and we don't even know which kind it was. The question must start there.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth vessel itself
They are unsure about it; it is an open question

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבָּנַן, עִשָּׂרוֹן גּוּפֵיהּ קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ:
phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, the tenth vessel itself is in question for them:
was it heaped, or was it leveled?
phrases.notes: חכמים had only one tenth vessel, so which kind it was is the first thing to figure out.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבָּנַן, עִשָּׂרוֹן גּוּפֵיהּ קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17's question about why only רבי מאיר was named.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For חכמים the doubt begins with the עשרון itself, so the half-tenth question fits רבי מאיר's view, where the עשרון is already clear.

steps.title: רב חסדא: רבי מאיר's own view gives the answer
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that we can learn the answer from רבי מאיר's own words, both for רבי מאיר and for חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: From רבי מאיר's view we can learn what רבי מאיר holds, and from רבי מאיר's view we can also learn what חכמים hold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers רמי בר חמא's question. He says no new source is needed, because רבי מאיר's known opinion already settles it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's ruling about which tenth vessel was used for what tells us what kind his half-tenth vessel was. That same ruling also shows what חכמים hold, so it answers the question that step 18 raised for them too.

keyTerms.meaning: We can learn it, we can figure it out
From רבי מאיר's own words

steps.whatToRemember: The half-tenth question is answered from inside רבי מאיר's own opinion. That same opinion also reveals what חכמים hold about the tenth and half-tenth vessels.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִדְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר נִשְׁמַע לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: He said to him: From Rabbi Meir we can learn about Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: From what רבי מאיר said about his two tenth vessels, we can tell what kind his half-tenth vessel was.

phrases.english: and from Rabbi Meir we can learn about the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב חסדא's answer to the question from step 15, and covers the חכמים issue from step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר's own stated view settles the half-tenth question for him, and also shows what חכמים hold.

steps.title: The half-tenth vessel was leveled, by רבי מאיר and by the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains his answer. Since רבי מאיר says the tenth vessel was leveled, the half-tenth vessel was also leveled. And since that is true for רבי מאיר, it is also true for the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי מאיר said the tenth vessel was measured leveled, the half-tenth vessel was also leveled. And since by רבי מאיר it was leveled, by the רבנן it was also leveled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא spells out the proof he promised in the previous step. He uses רבי מאיר's own ruling to answer the question for both opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר clearly says the tenth vessel was leveled. Both vessels belong to the same offering, so the half-tenth should work the same way. The רבנן's open question was about the tenth vessel, and that is now settled the same way: leveled.

keyTerms.meaning: Leveled: filled with the extra scraped off flat, not heaped up
A tenth of an איפה; also the name of the vessel that holds that amount
Half of a tenth; the smaller measuring vessel

steps.whatToRemember: By both רבי מאיר and the רבנן, the vessels used for the חביתי כהן גדול measured leveled.

phrases.english: From the fact that רבי מאיר said:
the tenth vessel is leveled,
the half-tenth vessel is also leveled;
and from the fact that according to רבי מאיר it is leveled,
according to the רבנן it is also leveled.
phrases.notes: For the רבנן, the open question was about the tenth vessel itself (step 18). This line answers that too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind רב חסדא's answer in step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leveled, both for רבי מאיר and for the רבנן

steps.title: How were the חביתין divided into loaves: by hand or with a vessel?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks the second question in the סימן. Was the dough of the חביתי כהן גדול divided into its loaves by hand, or with a measuring vessel?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: the חביתי כהן גדול, how does one divide them into loaves? By hand or with a vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens, the 'griddle-cakes' item from the סימן. רמי בר חמא wants to know how the dough was split into the separate loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offering is one batch of flour that must become several equal loaves. The question is whether the כהן just estimated the portions by hand, or measured them exactly with a tool.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily griddle-cake offering of the כהן גדול, brought half in the morning and half in the afternoon
Loaves or cakes
By hand or with a vessel

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: רמי בר חמא asked of רב חסדא:
the griddle-cakes of the כהן גדול,
with what does one divide them into loaves,
by hand or with a vessel?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the second question listed in the סימן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חביתין dough was divided by hand or measured with a vessel

steps.title: Obviously by hand, since we would not bring scales in
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that it is obviously done by hand. If it were done with a measuring tool, would one bring scales into the עזרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that it is by hand. For if it were with a vessel, would he bring in scales?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. He says it must be by hand, because the other option would mean bringing scales into the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting exactly equal loaves with a tool would mean weighing them. רב חסדא treats bringing scales in as plainly unacceptable, so the division must be done by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
Scales for weighing
He would bring in

phrases.english: It is obvious that it is by hand,
for if with a vessel, would he bring in scales?!
phrases.notes: He means bringing scales into the עזרה, the Temple courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By hand, because dividing with a vessel would mean bringing scales in

steps.title: So let him bring scales in
steps.stepSummary: A challenge comes back: what is wrong with bringing scales in?
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him bring them in!
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is challenged. Why is bringing scales into the מקדש so unthinkable?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's answer assumed scales do not belong in the מקדש, but he never gave a reason. This one word pushes him to explain what is actually wrong with them.

keyTerms.meaning: So let him bring it in

phrases.english: So let him bring them in!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that scales cannot be brought into the מקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No reason was given for forbidding scales, so why not use them?

steps.title: Weighing bread is written as a curse, so it is not fitting
steps.stepSummary: The answer: weighing bread is written in the תורה as part of a curse, so it is not proper conduct to do it in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is written as part of a curse, it is not proper conduct.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered. Bread by weight shows up in the תוכחה as a sign of hunger, so it does not fit the honor of the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scales are not technically forbidden. The issue is that weighing bread recalls a curse of famine, and that is not respectful behavior in the מקדש. So the division stays by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: A curse; here the curses in the תוכחה
Proper, respectful conduct

steps.whatToRemember: The חביתין were divided by hand, because weighing bread is a sign of a curse.

phrases.english: Since it is written as part of a curse,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:26: 'they shall bring back your bread by weight.'

phrases.english: it is not proper conduct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason behind the assumption: respect for the מקדש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Scales could be brought in, since nothing forbids them
steps.terutzMaskana: Weighing bread recalls a curse, so it is not fitting; the division is by hand

steps.title: Does the שלחן make holy קמצים placed on its upper part?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks the third question in the סימן. Does the שלחן make holy קמצים placed on its upper part? Maybe it does, since it makes the לחם הפנים holy. Or maybe it only makes holy what belongs on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: the שלחן, does it make holy קמצים placed on its heaped-up upper part? Since it makes bread holy, does it also make קמצים holy? Or perhaps it makes holy what is fit for it, and does not make holy what is not fit for it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens, the 'table' item from the סימן. רמי בר חמא lays out both sides of a doubt about whether the שלחן works like a כלי שרת for things that do not belong on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שלחן clearly makes holy the לחם הפנים placed on it. The doubt is whether that power reaches קמצים too, which are not its usual contents. Or does it only work on things that are meant to go on it?

keyTerms.meaning: The Table in the מקדש on which the לחם הפנים was placed
Handfuls taken from a מנחה, or of לבונה
The heaped-up upper part; here the space above the Table among the loaves
Makes holy
What is fit for it, what belongs on it
Or perhaps; introduces the other side of a doubt

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: רמי בר חמא asked of רב חסדא:
The Table, what is the law
as to whether it makes holy handfuls placed on its heaped-up part?
phrases.notes: He means handfuls that were never put into a proper vessel and were placed on the Table among the loaves instead.

phrases.english: Since it makes the bread holy,
does it also make handfuls holy,
or perhaps what is fit for it, it makes holy,
and what is not fit for it, it does not make holy?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא: שֻׁלְחָן מַהוּ שֶׁיְּקַדֵּשׁ קְמָצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the third question listed in the סימן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the שלחן makes holy only the bread that belongs on it, or also קמצים placed on it

steps.title: The Table does not make the handfuls holy
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers רמי בר חמא's third question: the שלחן does not make the קמצים holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It does not make them holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question about the שלחן. He says it does not make the קמצים holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 there were two sides: maybe the שלחן makes holy anything on it, or maybe only what belongs on it. רב חסדא picks the second side. The שלחן is meant for the לחם הפנים, not for קמצים, so it does not make them holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes holy. Here it means the vessel gives holiness to what is placed in it or on it
Handfuls taken from a מנחה, or of לבונה, to be burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: He said to him: It does not make them holy.
phrases.notes: רב חסדא is answering רמי בר חמא's question about the קמצים placed on the שלחן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 25
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the שלחן make holy קמצים put on it?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The שלחן does not make the קמצים holy.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוחנן: the Table makes holy far above it
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא challenges רב חסדא. רבי יוחנן said the שלחן makes holy everything stacked high above it, either fifteen or twelve טפחים up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But didn't רבי יוחנן say: According to the one who says the loaves are folded two and a half טפחים, it comes out that the שלחן makes holy fifteen טפחים above it. According to the one who says they are folded two טפחים, it comes out that the שלחן makes holy twelve טפחים above it.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא attacks רב חסדא's answer. He quotes רבי יוחנן, who says the שלחן's holiness reaches high above it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the שלחן makes holy the whole height of the stacked loaves, fifteen or twelve טפחים, depending on the opinion. If the שלחן's holiness reaches that far up, it seems it should also make holy קמצים placed on it. That would contradict רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word for a challenge
Folds. The edges of the לחם הפנים were folded up
A handbreadth, a unit of measurement
The special loaves arranged on the שלחן each שבת

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not arguing about how tall the loaves were for its own sake. The point the גמרא takes from him is that the שלחן gives holiness to things far above its surface.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
According to the one who says one folds two and a half handbreadths,
phrases.notes: The loaves were longer than the table, so their edges were folded up. The two opinions argue about how much was folded.

phrases.english: it comes out that the Table makes holy
fifteen handbreadths above it.
phrases.notes: Six loaves were stacked on each side. Six times two and a half makes fifteen.

phrases.english: According to the one who says one folds two handbreadths,
it comes out that the Table makes holy
twelve handbreadths above it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer in step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that the שלחן does not make the קמצים holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן says the שלחן makes holy everything stacked high above it. So it should also make holy קמצים placed on it.

steps.title: Holy enough to become פסול, not enough to be offered
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains himself. The שלחן does not make the קמצים holy enough to be offered on the מזבח, but it does make them holy enough to become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It does not make them holy to be offered, but it does make them holy to become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge by explaining what he meant. There are two levels of holiness, and the שלחן gives the קמצים only the lower one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא agrees that the שלחן gives some holiness, which fits רבי יוחנן. That holiness is enough for the קמצים to become פסול. It is not enough to let them be offered on the מזבח, and that is all he meant when he said 'it does not make them holy.'

keyTerms.meaning: To be offered on the מזבח
To become disqualified (פסול)

steps.whatToRemember: Holiness from a כלי שרת can come in two levels. One level only makes an item able to become פסול. A higher level makes it fit to be offered. The שלחן gives the קמצים only the first level.

phrases.english: He said to him: It does not make them holy to be offered,
but it does make them holy to become disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ מְקַדֵּשׁ לִיקְרַב, אֲבָל מְקַדֵּשׁ לִיפָּסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by narrowing what step 26 meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed רב חסדא meant the שלחן gives the קמצים no holiness at all, which would contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שלחן gives holiness that lets the קמצים become פסול, but not holiness that makes them fit to be offered.

steps.title: The seven liquid measures in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists the seven vessels used in the מקדש to measure liquids: a הין, half a הין, a third of a הין, a quarter of a הין, a לוג, half a לוג, and a quarter of a לוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There were seven measures for liquids in the מקדש: a הין, half a הין, a third of a הין, and a quarter of a הין; a לוג, half a לוג, and a quarter of a לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the seven measuring vessels for liquids that were in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list has two groups. The first is the הין and its fractions: a הין is twelve לוג, so the fractions are six, four, and three לוג. The second is the לוג and its fractions, a half and a quarter.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Marks the start of a new משנה
Measuring vessels for liquids, such as oil and wine
A large liquid measure, equal to twelve לוג
A smaller liquid measure
A quarter

steps.whyThisMatters: These measures were used to get the exact amounts of oil and wine for מנחות and נסכים. The coming גמרא will discuss what each vessel was used for.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁל לַח הָיוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: There were seven measures for liquids in the Temple:
a hin, and half a hin,
and a third of a hin, and a quarter of a hin.
A log, and half a log, and a quarter of a log.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁל לַח הָיוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after רמי בר חמא's questions are finished
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מקדש had seven liquid measuring vessels: a הין, ½ הין, ⅓ הין, ¼ הין, a לוג, ½ לוג, and ¼ לוג.

steps.title: One hin vessel with marked lines
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בר רבי צדוק says the הין vessel had marked lines showing the amount needed for a bull, a ram and a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בר רבי צדוק says: There were marked lines on the הין vessel: up to here is for the bull, up to here is for the ram, and up to here is for the lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה argues with the list of seven separate vessels from the previous step. It says one הין vessel with lines on it did the job of several vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion counted half a הין, a third of a הין and a quarter of a הין as separate vessels. רבי אליעזר בר רבי צדוק says these amounts were measured inside the one הין vessel, using lines marked for the bull, the ram and the lamb. So he did not need three extra vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: Marked lines on a vessel showing set amounts
A liquid measure equal to 12 לוגין
A bull offering
A ram offering
A lamb offering

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
There were marked lines on the hin vessel,
up to here is for the bull,
phrases.notes: These are the amounts of wine poured with each animal: half a הין for a bull, a third for a ram, a quarter for a lamb (במדבר 28:14).

phrases.english: and up to here is for the ram,
up to here is for the lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's list of separate vessels for the parts of a הין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The parts of a הין were measured with one marked הין vessel, not with separate vessels.

steps.title: No hin vessel, but a vessel of a log and a half
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says there was no full הין vessel, since a full הין was never needed. The seventh vessel was a measure of a לוג and a half, used for the מנחת כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: There was no הין vessel there. What would a הין vessel be used for? Rather, there was an extra measure of a לוג and a half there. With it he would measure the oil for the מנחת כהן גדול: a לוג and a half in the morning, and a לוג and a half in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the משנה. רבי שמעון takes the full הין off the list and puts a vessel of a לוג and a half in its place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's reasoning is practical: no offering ever needed a full הין, so there was no reason to have that vessel. He still keeps the count at seven by adding a measure of a לוג and a half. That was the amount of oil needed for each half of the כהן גדול's daily מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra measuring vessel
A smaller liquid measure; there are 12 in a הין
The daily meal offering of the כהן גדול, offered half in the morning and half in the afternoon
Afternoon, toward evening

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
There was no hin vessel there,
for what would a hin vessel be used for?
phrases.notes: He means that no offering needed exactly a full הין, so that vessel would have had no use.

phrases.english: Rather, an extra measuring vessel
of a log and a half was there,
with which he would measure
for the meal offering of the High Priest:
a log and a half in the morning,
a log and a half in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיָה שָׁם הִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view in the משנה, removing the הין vessel from the first opinion's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There was no הין vessel. Instead there was a vessel of a לוג and a half for the מנחת כהן גדול.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three views: seven separate vessels including a הין; one marked הין vessel (רבי אליעזר בר רבי צדוק); and no הין vessel but a vessel of a לוג and a half (רבי שמעון).

steps.title: רבי יהודה lists the seven vessels from smallest to largest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה lists the seven liquid measures, starting from a quarter לוג and going up to a full הין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: There were seven measures for liquids in the מקדש: a quarter לוג, a half לוג, a לוג, a quarter הין, a third of a הין, a half הין, and a הין. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא about the same seven vessels. It starts with רבי יהודה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה lists the same seven vessels as the first opinion in the משנה, but he counts upward, from the smallest to the largest. This sets up the next step, where רבי מאיר lists them in the opposite order.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and explains the משנה
Measuring vessels for liquids
A quarter of a לוג, the smallest vessel
A quarter of a הין, which equals 3 לוגין

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
Seven measures for liquid
were in the Temple:
a quarter log, a half log, and a log,
a quarter hin, a third of a hin,
a half hin, and a hin,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁל לַח הָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same list of vessels from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the seven vessels, from smallest to largest, are: quarter לוג, half לוג, לוג, quarter הין, third הין, half הין, הין.

steps.title: רבי מאיר lists the same vessels from largest to smallest
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר lists the same seven vessels, but starts from the full הין and goes down to a quarter לוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: a הין, a half הין, a third of a הין, a quarter הין, a לוג, a half לוג, and a quarter לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי מאיר's version of the list. It has the same vessels as רבי יהודה's list, in the opposite order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No vessel is added or removed here. The only difference from רבי יהודה is the order: רבי מאיר counts down from the largest vessel instead of up from the smallest.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a הין, which equals 6 לוגין
A third of a הין, which equals 4 לוגין
Half a לוג

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a different set of vessels here. רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר list exactly the same seven vessels. Only the order is different.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
a hin, a half hin, a third of a hin,
a quarter hin, a log,
a half log, and a quarter log.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הִין, וַחֲצִי הִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the same list as רבי יהודה in reverse order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the seven vessels, from largest to smallest, are: הין, half הין, third הין, quarter הין, לוג, half לוג, quarter לוג.

steps.title: רבי שמעון in the ברייתא: no הין vessel
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא also brings רבי שמעון's view, the same one we saw in the משנה: there was no full הין vessel, because it had no use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: There was no הין vessel there. What would a הין vessel be used for?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds רבי שמעון's objection to having a full הין vessel, matching his view in the משנה. His statement continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not just a repeat of the משנה. It is part of the ברייתא, which records רבי שמעון disagreeing with both רבי יהודה's and רבי מאיר's lists, since both of them include a full הין.

keyTerms.meaning: Serves, is used for
"For what…?" A question meaning there is no reason for it

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
There was no hin vessel there,
for what would a hin vessel be used for?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיָה שָׁם הִין, וְכִי מָה הָיָה הִין מְשַׁמֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with both רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר, since both include a full הין vessel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There was no full הין vessel in the מקדש, because no offering needed that amount.
